story_type: floatplane crash on Kodiak Island, beacon alert, two helicopters rescue three
hook: This floatplane crashed in the Alaska wilderness.
narration: This floatplane crashed and ended up on its side, with three people aboard.
It went down near Uganik Lake on Kodiak Island, Alaska, in September 2016.
Planes like this carry a beacon that starts transmitting by itself in a crash, and its alert reached the Coast Guard at twenty past noon.
Air Station Kodiak launched two rescue helicopters.
A rescue swimmer rode the cable down to the crash site.
[short pause] On the beach below, the three survivors waited with the rescue crew.
outcome: The two Kodiak helicopter crews rescued all three people from the crash.
title: Floatplane crash on Kodiak Island
description:
On Sept. 9, 2016, two Coast Guard Air Station Kodiak helicopter crews rescued three people after their De Havilland DHC-2 floatplane crashed near Uganik Lake on Kodiak Island, Alaska. An electronic locator beacon alert brought them in.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video, Air Station Kodiak, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/482342
